title: Target transition above a thickening
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $q\in\mathbf Z$. Let $i:T_1\to T_2$ be a closed immersion of schemes surjective on points [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $e_2:Y_2\to T_2$, $h_2:Y_2\to X$, $a:Y_1\to Y_2$, $e_1:Y_1\to T_1$, and $h_1:Y_1\to X$ satisfy $h_2a=h_1$, with the square $e_2a=i e_1$ cartesian. For any etale sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_2$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the canonical transition between the degree-$q$ targets of [sbc-def-base-change-map], $R^qh_{2,*}e_2^{-1}F\to R^qh_{1,*}e_1^{-1}i^{-1}F$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, condition (1): thickenings; transition compatibility made explicit

proof.text: The cartesian square makes a a base change of i, hence a closed immersion surjective on points. These two properties are stable under base change (the corresponding Mathlib scheme morphism instances).

Apply [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site] to a. Its derived pullback adjunction is an equivalence, so its unit is invertible. The transition Rh2_* to Rh1_*a^{-1} is the direct image of that unit followed by the composition isomorphism. To see the derived equivalence directly, apply the additive equivalence and its exact inverse degreewise to bounded-below complexes: they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and their inverse natural isomorphisms descend to the localization. For the identification of the transition, use the composite-unit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the conjugate-defined right-adjoint comparison [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Substitute these formulas; naturality moves the intervening counit past the unit, and the triangle identity cancels the unit-counit pair for g (respectively h2). The remaining map is the direct image of the invertible unit for i (respectively a).
The cartesian comparison identifies a^{-1}e2^{-1} with e1^{-1}i^{-1}. All coefficient and single-complex comparisons are isomorphisms, and degree-q homology preserves them.
